common_name: Whopper Red Bronze Leaf Begonia (Large-Leaved Vigorous Landscape Begonia)

planting.note: Set out rooted transplants after all frost danger has passed into fertile, well-drained soil in partial shade to shade. This interspecific hybrid is sold as vegetatively propagated plugs rather than seed.

directions: Whopper Red Bronze Leaf bears large clusters of bright red flowers over glossy, bronze-tinted foliage on a substantially larger plant than standard wax begonias, part of an interspecific hybrid group bred for bold mass-planting impact. It blooms continuously from planting through frost without deadheading and shrugs off summer heat and humidity better than older bedding begonias. Space plants generously, since individual specimens fill out into a broad, rounded mound. Treat as an annual outside its tender perennial zone range and water during dry spells to keep the glossy foliage from scorching.

common_name: Whopper Rose Green Leaf Begonia (Large-Leaved Vigorous Landscape Begonia)

planting.note: Set out rooted transplants after all frost danger has passed into fertile, well-drained soil in partial shade to shade; the plain green-leaved counterpart to Whopper Rose Bronze Leaf.

directions: Whopper Rose Green Leaf produces abundant clusters of clear rose-pink flowers over plain glossy green foliage, giving a lighter, brighter look in the border than its bronze-leaved sibling. Like other Whopper-series begonias it grows into an unusually large, vigorous mound for a bedding begonia and keeps flowering nonstop from spring planting until frost. It handles heat and humidity well and needs little more than regular watering and an occasional feeding to perform at its best. Use it as a bold filler among shrubs or taller shade perennials where a smaller wax begonia would be lost.

common_name: Kauai White Wishbone Flower (Compact Early-Blooming White Torenia)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost and transplant into moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade after frost danger passes; Kauai White is the pure-white, yellow-throated member of this compact, early-flowering wishbone flower series.

directions: Kauai White bears crisp white, snapdragon-like flowers marked with a bright yellow throat spot on a tidy, mounding plant that begins flowering earlier in the season than older torenia strains. It thrives in deep shade where few other flowering annuals perform, blooming continuously from late spring through frost without any deadheading. Keep the soil evenly moist through summer heat, since torenia wilts quickly if it dries out, and work compost into beds beforehand to hold moisture. Its pale color brightens dim corners and pairs well with the deeper blues and burgundies sold alongside it in the same series.

common_name: SunPatiens Compact Tropical Rose Impatiens (Sun-Tolerant Season-Long Bedding Impatiens)
scientific_name: Impatiens x hybrida 'SunPatiens Compact Tropical Rose' (SAKIMP037)

planting.note: Set out vegetatively propagated transplants after the last frost into fertile, well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun; Tropical Rose carries variegated green-and-yellow foliage behind its pink blooms.

directions: SunPatiens Compact Tropical Rose forms a dense, self-branching mound of variegated green-and-yellow foliage topped with pink flowers accented by darker red centers, adding ornamental interest even between flushes of bloom. It holds up to heat and sun far better than old-fashioned impatiens walleriana while still performing well in the partial shade of a porch or tree canopy. Because it carries resistance to impatiens downy mildew, it is a dependable substitute in beds where that disease has wiped out plantings of Impatiens walleriana. Feed on a regular schedule and keep soil evenly moist, since the compact habit has less root volume to draw on during hot, dry stretches.

common_name: SunPatiens Compact Royal Magenta Impatiens (Sun-Tolerant Season-Long Bedding Impatiens)
scientific_name: Impatiens x hybrida 'SunPatiens Compact Royal Magenta'

planting.note: Set out vegetatively propagated transplants after the last frost into fertile, well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun; Royal Magenta is a solid-color selection within the compact tier of the SunPatiens line.

directions: Royal Magenta smothers itself in vivid magenta-pink flowers over plain green foliage, holding a tight, mounded habit that needs no pinching to stay full. It tolerates far more direct sun than Impatiens walleriana yet still flowers heavily in the partial shade of eaves, pergolas, or high tree canopy where many sun annuals falter. Its resistance to impatiens downy mildew makes it a reliable choice in regions where that disease has made traditional impatiens risky to plant. Water deeply during dry spells and feed monthly to sustain the dense, continuous bloom from spring planting through the first frost.

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost and transplant after frost danger passes into moist, well-drained soil in shade to partial shade. Avoid overhead watering to reduce the risk of impatiens downy mildew.

directions: Accent White produces pure white, 1.5-inch flowers in profusion over a compact, basal-branching mound, brightening the deepest shade without any deadheading required. It shares the Accent series' free-flowering habit and tolerance of the low-light conditions under trees and on north-facing foundations where few other annuals bloom reliably. Grow it in humus-rich, evenly moist soil and provide good air circulation, since Impatiens walleriana is prone to impatiens downy mildew in damp, crowded plantings. Its clean white color makes it a popular choice for moon gardens and as a unifying color among mixed shade containers.

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost and transplant after frost danger passes into moist, well-drained soil in shade to partial shade. Avoid overhead watering to reduce the risk of impatiens downy mildew.

directions: Accent Burgundy bears deep wine-red flowers on the same compact, mounded habit as the rest of the Accent series, giving a richer, more saturated color option for shaded borders and containers. It flowers continuously from planting through frost without deadheading, and its natural woodland origin gives it genuine tolerance for the dense shade under trees and shrubs. Plant in fertile, consistently moist soil and space plants to allow airflow, since crowded, damp conditions encourage impatiens downy mildew. The dark flower color shows up best against light-colored foliage companions such as caladium or variegated hosta.

planting.note: Start seed indoors 10-12 weeks before the last frost and transplant after frost danger passes into moist, well-drained soil in shade to partial shade; Super Elfin XP is bred for a tight flowering window so mixed-color flats finish uniformly.

directions: Super Elfin XP White covers itself in clean white blooms on a dwarf, uniform mound slightly more compact than the Accent series, making it a long-time standard for shaded bedding displays, window boxes, and hanging baskets. The XP breeding line was developed for a narrow, predictable flowering window so growers can ship entire crops of mixed colors in bloom at once. It performs best in consistently moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil and benefits from good air circulation to limit impatiens downy mildew. No deadheading is needed to keep flowers coming from spring planting through the first fall frost.

common_name: Grandiflora Flowering Tobacco (Fragrant Evening-Blooming White Nicotiana)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost, since it needs light to germinate and should only be lightly pressed into the surface of the mix; transplant into humus-rich soil in partial shade after frost danger passes.

directions: Grandiflora is an old heirloom strain of flowering tobacco bearing large, creamy white, intensely fragrant trumpet flowers that open wide in the evening and on overcast days, closing up again in strong afternoon sun. Its tall, somewhat sprawling habit and powerful jasmine-like scent make it best suited to the back of a border or near a porch or window where its evening perfume can be enjoyed, and light shade actually helps keep the flowers open longer through the day. Grow in humus-rich, evenly moist soil and stake taller stems in windy sites, since the plant can become leggy in deep shade. Deadhead faded flowers to tidy the plant and limit excessive self-seeding, since it readily naturalizes in favorable climates.
sources: North Carolina State Extension (NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox)

common_name: Heart to Heart Chinook Caladium (Salmon-Pink Strap-Leaf Caladium)

planting.note: Plant tubers after all frost danger has passed once soil has warmed above 65F; Chinook is part of the Heart to Heart series bred for improved sun tolerance alongside classic shade performance.

directions: Chinook carries elongated, strap-shaped leaves in a warm salmon-pink overlaid with deeper pink veining and edged in a crisp dark green border, with the coloring intensifying toward coral in brighter light and fading to a softer pastel pink in deeper shade. As a strap-leaf type its narrower, sturdier foliage resists tearing in wind and rain better than large fancy-leaf caladiums, making it a good choice for exposed containers. Plant tubers knobby-side up in rich, well-drained soil and keep consistently moist through the growing season, since caladiums sulk and go dormant early if allowed to dry out. Lift and store tubers over winter in zones below its hardiness range, or discard and replant fresh tubers each spring.
sources: Proven Winners -- Heart to Heart Caladiums
